test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 04 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which statement best differentiates ROM from RAM in terms of volatility and usage?

options.text: RAM is volatile and stores temporary data; ROM is non-volatile and stores boot instructions
ROM is used for multitasking; RAM is used for storing BIOS.
ROM is volatile and used for running programs; RAM is non-volatile and stores firmware.
RAM is permanent; ROM is temporary.

solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM is volatile and stores temporary data; ROM is non-volatile and stores boot instructions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a volatile memory that temporarily stores data being used by the CPU during system operation.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is non-volatile and retains data even when the computer is turned off.
 
• RAM is designed for high-speed data access and enables the smooth functioning of active applications and tasks.
 
• ROM stores critical data like the computer’s firmware or boot instructions, which are essential for initiating the system.
 
• RAM is writable and erasable, whereas ROM contains pre-written data that cannot be modified easily.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile Memory (e.g., RAM)**

 
 
• Power: Needs continuous power to hold data.
 
• Speed: Very fast.
 
• Use: Temporary storage for running applications and active data.
 
• Examples: RAM (Random Access Memory), CPU Cache. 
 
 
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory (e.g., SSD, HDD)**
 
 
• Power: Retains data even without power.
 
• Speed: Slower than volatile memory.
 
• Use: Long-term storage for files, OS, software.
 
• Examples: SSDs, HDDs, USB drives, ROM (Read-Only Memory).
